name: Swervedriver
label: Creation Records
lede: Two Oxford schoolmates raised near a car plant put muscle-car riffs under shoegaze noise, then lost a drummer to a sandwich run at the Canadian border and their best-reviewed album to a label that dropped them a week after release.

eras.title: Shake Appeal, and a tape in a limo
eras.text: Adam Franklin and Jimmy Hartridge went to school near the British Leyland car plant in Oxford, and the cars stuck. Their teenage garage band made one single; the songs Franklin wrote after it got them a deal with Creation Records almost at once.

years.h: Franklin and Hartridge start Shake Appeal at school in Oxford
years.p: Franklin's older brother Graham sings and Paddy Pulzer drums. The models are late-'60s garage rock.

years.h: Adi Vines joins on bass
years.p: Shake Appeal's one single, 'Gimme Fever', comes out on Notown Records in 1988.

years.h: 'Son of Mustang Ford' and a move to London
years.p: Franklin writes it with 'Volcano Trash' and 'Afterglow', and the band demos them at Union Street Studios in Oxford. Graham Franklin and Pulzer leave; in London, Edinburgh drummer Graham Bonnar joins.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Vice: We Talked to Shoegaze Legends Swervedriver · Creation Records
years.h: Alan McGee signs them from the back of a limousine in Los Angeles
years.p: The demo reaches [[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]] through [[Mark Gardener|57f73c2e-ee2f-49d9-b3c6-839259bc7eba]] of [[Ride|3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e]]. McGee plays it riding around downtown LA and signs the band straight away.
years.xp:
Franklin tells a street-level version too: the band was walking into Blast First Records, saw the Creation people coming along the street, and thought, "rather than giving it to the other people we should just give it to these guys."

Hartridge, asked in 2008 about McGee's version of hearing the tape while driving across America: "I'm pretty sure that's factual," though he thought it was more likely along Sunset Boulevard.

eras.title: Son of Mustang Ford
eras.text: Three EPs in a year and a half, all made by the band in London studios, then a debut album that brought American alt-rock muscle into a scene known for staring at its shoes. By 1991 A&M Records had signed them for America.

years.h: The first EP is about a car, and the NME hears Hüsker Dü
years.p: Four tracks including 'Kill the Superheroes'. Simon Williams' NME review runs under the headline "Hüsker Düing it for the Kids".

years.h: Rave Down, EP number two
years.p: Like the first, recorded at the Greenhouse and Falconer studios in London and produced by the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Vice: We Talked to Shoegaze Legends Swervedriver
years.h: A&M signs them for the United States
years.p: A US major, for a band whose first EP came out about six months earlier.

years.h: 'Sandblasted' gets them into the UK chart at No. 67
years.p: The third EP's title track goes on to the album.

years.h: Raise, self-produced, reaches No. 44
years.p: Nine songs, three already out on EPs. Early UK vinyl came with a free 7-inch of instrumentals, and Newsday called it "guitar grunge in a good mood."

eras.title: A sandwich at the border
eras.text: The original rhythm section was gone inside seven months, one member at a Canadian checkpoint and one after a Swedish festival. The replacements came from two Camden bars, and Alan Moulder, who had worked with My Bloody Valentine, started producing.

years.big: He went to get a sandwich.
q: we left him at the border and left him money
years.h: Graham Bonnar gets off the bus at the Canadian border and doesn't come back
years.p: The band was waiting to cross into the US for a Toronto show. Dan Davis of Run Westy Run covers five dates, then Danny Ingram of D.C.'s Strange Boutique finishes the tour.
years.xp:
The band's account to L.A. Record: "He said he was going to go out and get a sandwich. And he didn't reappear." They left him at the border, with money.

Wikipedia gives the reason as artistic differences. Bonnar would be back behind the kit for Scandinavian shows in 2010.

years.h: Alan Moulder walks up to Franklin in a bar and offers to produce
years.p: The meeting is at the bar of ULU, the University of London Union. The result is the fourth EP, with 'The Watchmakers Hands' and 'Scrawl and Scream'.
years.xp:
Franklin, in 2018, on the approach: "I was like '...Yeah, who are you?' He said, 'My name's Alan Moulder, I produce records.'"

With the band down to Franklin and Hartridge, Franklin said, "we only really had half a band."

years.cap: Vines and Franklin at the Paradiso, Amsterdam, July 25, 1992
years.h: After Hultsfred in Sweden, Adi Vines quits for a metal band
years.p: He leaves to form Skyscraper. Franklin and Hartridge split the bass parts between them on the next album.

years.h: A drummer at the Murray Arms, a bassist at the next bar over
years.p: Jez Hindmarsh, introduced by producer Marc Waterman, offers his 16-track gear the same night in Camden. Steve George, from Essex, introduces himself to Franklin with a job pitch.
years.xp: George's opening line, as Wikipedia records it: "You're the guy from Swervedriver. You need a bass player. I'm your man."

years.src: Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Wikipedia: Mezcal Head · Louder
years.h: 'Duel' is Single of the Week in the NME and Melody Maker
years.p: It peaks at No. 60, their best UK placing. There are two videos: a snowboarding trip the band shot themselves on Mount Hood, and an MTV-made one in downtown Los Angeles.
years.xp:
Skyscraper, Adi Vines' new band, put out its debut single the same week. Swervedriver got the Single of the Week slots; Skyscraper didn't.

'Duel' and 'Last Train to Satansville' both ended up on the soundtrack of the 3DO game Road Rash, and 'Duel' turned up again in Burnout Paradise in 2008.

years.h: Five studios, two bassists, one Mezcal Head
years.p: Co-produced with Moulder, with Franklin and Hartridge covering bass. It reaches No. 55, and Pitchfork later puts it at No. 10 among the best shoegaze albums ever.

years.h: American arenas with the Smashing Pumpkins
years.p: Swervedriver tours the US with [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]] and [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]], two years after opening for [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]]. Franklin noticed crowds turning up early to see the opener.

eras.title: Dropped twice in a week
eras.text: The third album is the one critics hold up as their best. It came out in Britain and almost nowhere else, because the money that kept Swervedriver on Creation came from America, and America had pulled out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Wikipedia: Ejector Seat Reservation
years.h: The band wants 'The Other Jesus'; McGee picks 'Last Day on Earth'
years.p: McGee chooses the more Britpop-friendly song as the launch single. 'Bring Me the Head of the Fortune Teller' had come out in May.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Wikipedia: Ejector Seat Reservation
years.h: Bob Dylan's people say no to 'It's All Happening Now'
years.p: Promo copies are pulled when permission for lines from 'It's All Over Now, Baby Blue' is refused. The track goes only to the fan club.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ejector Seat Reservation · Wikipedia: Swervedriver
years.h: Ejector Seat Reservation, cut at the Church and Konk
years.p: Forty-five minutes, co-produced again with Moulder in Crouch End. AllMusic's Andy Kellman called it their "most cohesive and concise record."

years.src: Vice: We Talked to Shoegaze Legends Swervedriver · Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Creation Records
years.h: A week after release, Creation drops them too
years.p: A&M said the album wouldn't fit its schedule for 18 months, and the band asked to leave. Without the US licensing money, Creation let them go with no promotion.
years.xp:
Franklin to Vice in 2015: Creation "pulled out on the back of that because they weren't getting the massive amount of money from licensing us to A&M anymore." Wikipedia puts A&M's licensing at about $350,000 an album.

The record never came out in North America. Sony licensed it in Australia and brought the band over to tour.

Hartridge's view, in 2008, of why the album got so little push at home: "The label was not strong enough to deal with Oasis as well as all the other bands."

eras.title: Bad Earth and a three-hour goodbye
eras.text: A new American deal paid for a studio of their own in Farringdon. Then the label fired their A&R man and the band in the same afternoon, and Swervedriver put the record out themselves.

years.h: Geffen's DGC signs them for three albums, and they build Bad Earth
years.p: The studio in Farringdon, London, is where 99th Dream gets made, cut back from 48 tracks to 24 to thin out the guitars.

years.h: DGC lets their A&R man go, and drops the band three hours later
years.p: Promos already carried a May 7 release date. It's three and a half weeks out when Jody Kurilla loses his job in a downsizing.
years.xp:
Hindmarsh's read on it: "Someone from A&M once told us that it takes four or five listens to a Swervedriver album to see whether you like it or not." In that market, he said, a record that didn't hit immediately wasn't going to register.

Other majors were interested. The band went independent instead.

years.h: 99th Dream lands on Zero Hour in New York
years.p: The UK gets it on August 10, on the band's own Sonic Wave Discs. 'These Times' was re-recorded in December 1996 to lose its faster, Oasis-like first take. Entertainment Weekly missed "the sheer heaviness of the old Swervies," but heard a singular intensity.

years.cap: Poster for Hum and Swervedriver, Montreal, February 25, 1998
years.h: Opening for Hum at Irving Plaza, then out with Beck
years.p: The late-May North American run includes Sianspheric, [[The Dandy Warhols|5f572b31-8fd9-45ae-9beb-358c98d839df]] and [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]] before the tour moves to the UK in July.

years.h: The last show is at a brewery in Margaret River
years.p: Swervedriver opens for [[Powderfinger|e9ce3f55-b35c-4f8d-8304-be24f381587e]] at the Bootleg Brewery in Western Australia, and stops.
years.xp:
Franklin on the last year: "it cropped up, 'Is this fun? Are we having fun doing this?' I guess we kind of weren't."

By Wikipedia's account the band was burned out and tired of the drug scene around Bad Earth; they talked about selling the studio to [[Ash|99164692-c02d-407c-81c9-25d338dd21f4]] before the lease ran out. Hindmarsh started a management company, Hartridge a distribution business.

eras.title: Franklin keeps writing
eras.text: Franklin kept making records, as Toshack Highway and then under his own name. A 33-track anthology reminded him and Hartridge what they'd made, Hindmarsh self-published a tour memoir, Rider, and the Pixies' 2004 reunion made the idea of another go look less strange.

years.h: Two CDs from the original DATs, with four unreleased songs
years.p: Including the 1989 Shake Appeal demo of 'Son of Mustang Ford'. Franklin and Hartridge listened back and said, "Wow this is pretty great."

years.h: Franklin's Bolts of Melody, and a band with Interpol's drummer
years.p: His solo album comes out, and Magnetic Morning, with [[Sam Fogarino|0e48d6a9-7a38-42ae-9356-65ad8b6e977d]] of [[Interpol|b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e]], is under way.

years.h: A phone call in early October, and a 2008 tour is announced
years.p: Franklin and Hartridge talk it over, and Hindmarsh confirms on the band's forum: "Yep, it's true."

eras.title: Coachella first, new songs later
eras.text: The reunion started at a desert festival and ran in short tours for years. A new song on network television in 2012 led to the first albums since 1998, and a former Supergrass bassist who came in as a stand-in and stayed.

years.h: The comeback starts at Coachella
years.p: The classic four-piece opens a North American tour in Indio, California. In October, Sony BMG reissues Raise, Mezcal Head and Ejector Seat Reservation with bonus tracks.

years.h: Perth's arts festival, with Bonnar on drums
years.p: Bonnar had rejoined for Scandinavian dates the previous November. By June, Mikey Jones of Franklin's Bolts of Melody is the drummer.

years.cap: At the Key Club, West Hollywood, April 7, 2012
years.h: 'Deep Wound' on Jimmy Fallon, their first new song in 14 years
years.p: They play 'Son of Mustang Ford' too. A KEXP session in Seattle follows on April 4.

years.h: Raise in full across Australia, and 'Deep Wound' on 7-inch
years.p: Tym Records presses it in purple for presale and red and yellow for the tour. The band records new songs at Birdland in Melbourne when the dates end.

q: It feels great, I must say
years.src: Wikipedia: Swervedriver · Vice: We Talked to Shoegaze Legends Swervedriver
years.h: I Wasn't Born to Lose You, from Melbourne and Konk
years.p: Franklin credits the push to the others: Hartridge or George said they should write new material if they were going to keep playing.
play: I Wasn't Born to Lose You

years.h: Mick Quinn of Supergrass fills in on bass, and stays
years.p: Steve George can't make the US dates. Quinn is a full member by the time of the next album.

years.h: Future Ruins, on Dangerbird
years.p: Franklin, Hartridge, Jones and Quinn, the line-up that's stuck since.

years.h: The 99th Dream outtakes reach vinyl as Doremi Faso Latido
years.p: After Outer Battery's 2023 reissue of 99th Dream, the session demos and outtakes, once only on a 3CD set, get their own LP. A new EP, made with Ride's [[Mark Gardener|57f73c2e-ee2f-49d9-b3c6-839259bc7eba]] and Rick Beato, comes alongside.
years.xp:
Franklin on the EP: "We haven't really done an EP since our days with Creation."

He's known Hartridge, he says, since 1975.
